riscos.descricao: Respostas do Qwen afetadas por alucinações, incluindo afirmar que não tinha acesso aos arquivos fornecidos.
Ao aplicar a metodologia de tamanho 2 a CDs maiores, o Qwen alucinou completamente e o Claude Sonnet respondeu de forma muito genérica.
Contexto maior dificulta resposta correta e precisa, pois contexto adicional pode introduzir ruído.
Em alguns casos, a resposta sem RAG não era correta ou era inconclusiva.
Resultados preliminares da fase 1 com deficiências e imprevisibilidade.
Desvantagem do Qwen: necessidade de gerar 10 respostas, descartar manualmente as alucinadas e escolher a melhor; esforço não quantificado.
Depender do usuário para fornecer contexto preciso (por exemplo, qual dependência remover) sobrecarregaria o usuário; não quantificado.
Com o prompt NotDetailed, o LLM frequentemente propõe criar uma nova classe pouco motivada e menos aplicável que uma interface (qualidade/aplicabilidade da sugestão de refatoração).
Truncamento de partes do código com reticências nas sugestões, criticado por um desenvolvedor (código incompleto).
Privacidade/confidencialidade de dados ao usar modelo em nuvem: organizações podem não querer que seus dados sejam processados remotamente; não se trata de cibersegurança do código gerado.

citacoes.trecho: This study explores a first approach to use Large Language Models to suggest refactoring for architectural smells, with a focus on Cyclic Dependencies smells.
We study the use of detailed prompt and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to enhance LLMs, and we study local vs cloud LLMs.

In the first prompt(”NotDetailed”), the LLM is simply informed of the presence of a CD between two files, which are then passed to it within the prompt itself, carefully separated, so that the model can easily recognize the content of each file.
First, the LLM is asked to behave like an expert architectural software developer in AS.
The use of optimizers consists in improving the prompt by making it structured and organized by breaking down the information to be passed to the LLM into steps.
Before finalizing your answer, take a deep breath and review your reasoning to ensure the answer is accurate and complete.
citacoes.localizador: Seção III.E.a, regras do prompt Detailed, p. 4 do PDF (impressa 465)

citacoes.trecho: Subsequently, the edges that make up the dependency graph of the CD are described verbally (in Fig. 2 this step is represented by the ”Edges” entry).
This step was done by one of the authors, who viewed the CD through the dependencies graph and the files that generated it.
This allowed us to provide the LLM with specific terminology, definitions, examples and documentation related to CD refactoring.
Other two were obtained by varying the use of RAG and maintaining the same prompt and the same LLM.
Second Detailed/Qwen/RAG Detailed/Qwen/NotRag

citacoes.trecho: Therefore, after generating the ten answers, we chose the most relevant and understandable one and used it for the analysis.

As for the answers of Claude Sonnet, after some tests, where it was noted that it remained constant in the type of answer generated and always managed to grasp the data proposed, it was decided to generate a single answer for each scenario.
The problem of the management of greater context was split into two subproblems which are managed by two independent models, powered by the same LLM:
However, with the use of a multi-agent approach (in this case, two LLM-based agents with specific roles), seems to perform well and provide very good refactoring suggestions.

This was due to the fact that the answers of this model were affected by hallucinations [33] and sometimes the model was able to grasp the context (specifically, it stated that it was not aware of the files to be processed even though these were correctly provided).

In fact, when trying to apply the methodology used for size 2 CDs on larger CDs, the LLM Qwen was unable to give a meaningful response and was completely hallucinated, while Claude Sonnet responded in a very general way by often avoiding proposing solutions with an explicit lead.
However, the greater the context, the more difficult often is for the LLM to propose a correct and precise answer, as additional context can also introduce noise.
In some cases, however, the RAG answer was preferred because the one generated without the RAG was not correct at all or completely inconclusive.
These preliminary results were promising, although with various shortcomings and unpredictability.

A drawback of Qwen, however, is that, for each response generated, it was necessary to generate a total of 10, discard the completely hallucinated ones manually and choose the best of the remaining ones considering the coherence between the context of the question and the one of the answer.

We could argue that relying on the user to give such input (for example, specifying which dependency is better to remove) would burden the user and would require the user to have already solved the problem.

In fact, during the interviews, it was identified that through the use of the NotDetailed prompt, the LLM often tries to propose to create a new class, which is often not motivated appropriately, and the introduction of the latter is not as easily applicable as an interface.
The only detail that was not particularly appreciated by one of the developers, was the truncation, in the generated suggestions, of the code parts and the replacement with suspension points.
This can be a deal-breaker for some organizations that would not want to have their data processed by the LLM remotely.
By providing double opinions on some CDs during interviews with students, we tried to limit the subjectivity of such statements.
In fact, if the two students had stated contrasting answers, these CDs would not have been considered in the final result.
In fact, there are no tests on the behavior of Qwen through the use of the two different prompts and comparison tests between Claude 3.5 Sonnet and Qwen without the use of RAG.
